title: Flagged by a good test. Ill?
hook: The test catches 80% of cases and is 96% accurate. What does a flag mean?

knows: that accuracy can mislead when one class is rare
doesNotKnow: how to read what a positive flag means
the difference between precision and recall

misconception: A test that catches 80% of cases and is 96% accurate means a flagged person has about an 80% (or 96%) chance of being ill.
objective: The learner can explain that 'of those flagged, how many are ill' (precision) differs from 'of the ill, how many are flagged' (recall), and that a rare condition makes precision low even for an accurate test.

claims.text: Of 1,000 scans with 10 ill, a test that flags 8 of the ill and 40 of the 990 healthy flags 48 people, of whom 8 are ill: 16.7%.
claims.source: 8 / (8 + 40) = 0.1667. Reproduced by tally() in Demo.tsx (counts fixed by construction).

claims.text: The same test catches 80% of the ill (recall) and is right on 95.8% of scans (accuracy); flagging all 1,000 catches every ill person while a flag means ill 1% of the time.
claims.source: Recall 8 / 10; accuracy (8 + 950) / 1000; flag-all precision 10 / 1000. Reproduced by tally(PEOPLE, true/false) in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: The counts are invented for the toy; where the dots sit in the grid is a seeded shuffle.
claims.source: Brief 25 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md. Seed 7 into mulberry32 in population(); arbitrary, not tuned, and it changes no count (only dot positions).

claims.text: Precision is the share of flagged cases that are truly positive; recall is the share of truly positive cases that are flagged.
claims.source: Manning, Raghavan & Schütze 2008, Introduction to Information Retrieval, §8.3 (precision, recall, accuracy).

recall.question: A fraud model catches 90% of fraud, but fraud is 1 in 1,000 payments and the model also flags 2% of honest ones. A payment is flagged. Is it probably fraud?
options: No: most flags are honest payments
recall.why: Per 1,000 payments it flags about 0.9 frauds and about 20 honest ones, so under 5% of flags are fraud. Catching most fraud (recall) says little about what a flag means (precision) when fraud is rare.
